verdict.summary: Anyone can add an OAuth consumer in a Bitbucket workspace's settings and any Bitbucket user can authorize it immediately: there's no review or marketplace gate for plain OAuth 2.0. Since 4 May 2026 Atlassian enforces rotating refresh tokens, header-only Bearer tokens sent to api.bitbucket.org, and a 'scope' (not 'scopes') field in token responses, so older client code breaks.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Add a consumer with a callback URL, pick scopes, run the authorization code flow. No verification step is documented.

timeToProd.assumes: A 3LO OAuth consumer requesting repository and pullrequest scopes to read code and PRs on users' behalf; no Atlassian Marketplace listing.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs describe no approval step for OAuth consumers; absence of review is our reading.

prerequisites.item: A Bitbucket Cloud account and a workspace to own the consumer
prerequisites.why: Consumers are created under Workspace settings > Apps and features > OAuth consumers on any existing workspace.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The required workspace role isn't stated.

prerequisites.why: Required for OAuth 2.0 consumers; any callback sent in a request must sit under the configured URL.

prerequisites.item: Client code that sends tokens only in the Authorization header to https://api.bitbucket.org
prerequisites.why: Query-parameter and POST-body tokens and token calls to bitbucket.org are rejected after 4 May 2026.

scopeTiers.impact: Read the user's account and email. Enough for sign-in only.
Clone and browse repositories, read and comment on PRs. Note repository alone doesn't include PRs; pullrequest implies repository read.
Push, create/merge/decline PRs and run pipelines. pullrequest:write implicitly grants repository:write.
Repo/project admin, deletion, webhooks and pipeline variables. No review, but users see broad permissions on consent and only admins can use them.

steps.title: Open the workspace's OAuth consumer settings
steps.detail: Avatar > pick the workspace > Settings cog > Workspace settings > Apps and features > OAuth consumers (shown as 'OAuth clients' in some current UIs).

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 'OAuth clients' rename is from a third-party forum, not Atlassian.

steps.title: Add the consumer
steps.detail: Select Add consumer, enter a unique name, callback URL and scopes, save, then click the name to reveal the Key (client_id) and Secret.

steps.title: Choose least-privilege scopes
steps.detail: For a read-only code agent use repository + pullrequest (+ account); add pullrequest:write only if the agent opens or merges PRs.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Send users to https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&state=... and exchange the code with POST https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token (HTTP Basic client_id:secret, grant_type=authorization_code). Read 'scope' from the response.

steps.title: Handle rotating refresh tokens
steps.detail: Access tokens expire in one hour. Each refresh returns a new refresh token and the old one expires shortly after; unused refresh tokens expire after 3 months, forcing re-authorization.

steps.title: Call the API correctly
steps.detail: Send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' to https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/... ; clone with https://x-token-auth:{token}@bitbucket.org/... .

steps.title: Budget for per-user rate limits
steps.detail: Repository data endpoints allow 1,000 requests/hour per user by default (rolling). Watch X-RateLimit-NearLimit and cache aggressively.

steps.title: Test with a second Bitbucket account
steps.detail: Authorize from an account outside your workspace to confirm third-party access and refresh behaviour.

agentCanDo: Pick minimal scopes from the scope reference
Implement the code exchange and rotating refresh-token storage
Send header-only Bearer calls to api.bitbucket.org
Add rate-limit monitoring with X-RateLimit headers
Migrate older code off OAuth 1.0, implicit grant and app passwords
humanMustDo: Sign in and add the OAuth consumer in workspace settings
Copy and store the Key and Secret
Authorize once with a test account

blockers.symptom: 401s on API calls that worked before May 2026
blockers.cause: Tokens sent as query parameters or in the POST body, or requests sent to bitbucket.org instead of api.bitbucket.org.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails after a previous refresh succeeded
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens now rotate; the old token expires shortly after use.
blockers.fix: Persist the new refresh token from every refresh response.

blockers.symptom: Granted scopes appear empty after token exchange

blockers.cause: Token request missing or using an unsupported grant_type (implicit and password grants are gone).

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with an empty POST to the token endpoint on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: Users see the consent screen on every authorization
blockers.cause: Reported since late July 2026; no Atlassian response yet.
blockers.fix: Avoid unnecessary re-authorization by refreshing tokens rather than re-running the flow.

blockers.cause: Per-user hourly limit (1,000/hour for repository data by default).
blockers.fix: Back off, cache, and use webhooks instead of polling.

nuances.text: OAuth 1.0 and the implicit grant were retired on 27 February 2026; app passwords were scheduled to stop working on 9 June 2026 in favour of API tokens.
Client credentials grants no longer return refresh tokens, authenticate as an app_user, and consumers owned by personal workspaces only reach that workspace's data.
Scaled rate limits (up to 10,000/hour) apply only to workspace/project/repository access tokens and Forge asApp calls on large paid workspaces, not to per-user OAuth tokens.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The page lists those token types as requirements; OAuth 3LO isn't mentioned.

nuances.text: Bitbucket has no OIDC discovery document; it's plain OAuth 2.0.
The 'repository' scope doesn't include pull requests; request 'pullrequest' for PR data.
